note: Elixir has no export-list statement, so the public surface is read off the declarations: `def`/`defmacro`/`defguard`/`defdelegate` are public and `defp`/`defmacrop`/`defguardp` are not. That is a DIFFERENT statement from `contains` ('is a member') — it is the set another module can call as `Mod.f(...)`, which is what `bb_migrate`'s cross-language mapping and the go/java/kotlin exports edges are for; the go lane publishes `pkg -> CapitalizedName` at 1.0 on the declaration's own line and this does the same. A struct and a struct field are NOT exports (`%Mod{}` already produces `instantiates`).
